Saved-analysis migration and finite-sample interval notes

Source: vignettes/articles/mfrmr-technical-and-migration-notes.Rmd
mfrmr-technical-and-migration-notes.Rmd

This specialist guide archives two extended reference notes that accompany the installed help dictionary:

  1. Updating saved analyses from 0.2.x to 0.3.0: which saved objects can be re-summarized or replotted directly, which derived objects require recomputation from a saved fit, and which early numerical edge cases call for refitting from original rating data.
  2. Finite-sample normal-model interval evaluations: bounded simulation and exact-binomial summaries motivating the explicit status and CoverageQualified flags in confint.mfrm_multivariate_d_study(), confint.mfrm_multivariate_gstudy(), and confint.mfrm_fair_average().

For the 0.3.0 function and plot() migration tables, see ?mfrmr_api_migration_030 and compatibility_alias_table(). For model equations, spec and control keys, and return-object provenance, see ?fit_mfrm_technical_details.

1. Updating saved analyses from 0.2.x

Installing an updated version of mfrmr does not recalculate tables, figures, or reports already stored on disk. Keep the original objects, data, and analysis settings:

  • Native MFRM fits: print summary(fit) first and inspect its interpretation decision. If an early saved fit lacks current terminal-gradient or category-support records, refit from the original data with the same intended model, category coding, anchors, weights, and numerical controls. Running diagnose_mfrm() alone cannot supply estimation checks absent from the source fit.
  • Diagnostics and QC: recreate diagnose_mfrm() results with the original diagnostic settings (calculation_version = 2) before rebuilding reliability, precision, category, marginal-fit, person-fit, unexpected-response, fair-score, and consolidated report outputs. To reproduce earlier conventions explicitly, set fit_df_method = "engine", whexact = "legacy_linear", abs_z_min = 2, rule = "either", or pairwise df_method = "classical".
  • Model comparisons: rerun compare_mfrm() on eligible fits to apply the corrected RSM/PCM interaction-nesting check, then rebuild build_model_choice_review() and build_weighting_review().
  • Group comparisons, drift, and equivalence: recreate analyze_dff(), dif_interaction_table(), detect_anchor_drift(), build_equating_chain(), estimate_bias(), and estimate_all_bias() from the saved fits and original grouping inputs (method = "refit" in analyze_dff() reruns subgroup estimation to retain shared-Person and cell-count checks). Recompute analyze_facet_equivalence() from an eligible MML fit with matching diagnostics.
  • ICC, nesting, and rating-count reviews: rerun compute_facet_icc(), compute_facet_design_effect(), analyze_hierarchical_structure(), detect_facet_nesting(), and facet_small_sample_review() from the saved fit or original data to record data_identity, weighted-frequency pair accounting (UsedRows / ExcludedRows), and lowest-band WorstCategory summaries. In mfrm_report(fit, type = "checklist"), the count screen item is named "Facet rating-count screening".
  • G-Study and D-Study objects: saved 0.2.x G-Study and D-Study RDS objects work directly with mfrm_d_study(), summary(), plot(), and supported confint() methods. Rerun mfrm_d_study() from the saved G-Study when metric-specific G / Phi / SEM availability flags or new composite weights are needed; refit mfrm_g_study() only when changing the source data, switching to an explicit nesting specification, or replacing early single-score MINQUE(0) or period-containing interaction IDs.
  • Shrinkage, scoring, plausible values, and multiple imputation: reapply apply_empirical_bayes_shrinkage() (shrink_person = TRUE applies only to ordinary JML), rerun predict_mfrm_units(), score_mfrm_calibration(), score_mfrm_persons(), or sample_mfrm_plausible_values() when continuous centered-likelihood posterior intervals or fit_identity records are needed, and rerun pool_mfrm_imputed() on saved fit_mfrm_imputed() objects to attach IntervalReason notes without repeating imputations.
  • Agreement and rater networks: regenerate diagnose_mfrm(), then rebuild interrater_agreement_table(), rater_network_analysis(), rater_halo_network_analysis(), build_mfrm_network_review(), and mantel_haenszel_table() so ExpectedReason and Person-repeat dependency audits are recorded.

2. Finite-sample interval notes for G-Study and D-Study plans

The normal-model evaluations below summarize bounded numerical checks for the explicit methods in ?confint.mfrm_multivariate_d_study and ?confint.mfrm_multivariate_gstudy. Coverage figures count unavailable intervals in the planned denominator unless noted otherwise; they motivate explicit method selection and status inspection rather than certifying uniform finite-sample coverage across arbitrary designs or nonnormal ordinal scores.

Two-crossed-facet MLS null inversion (method = "mls")

  • In a matched 400-source normal-model check with 60 Persons, 4 raters, 12 tasks, and variance components (1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.3, 0.4, 0.1, 1) (ordered Person, Rater, Task, Person:Rater, Person:Task, Rater:Task, residual), the source-plan G interval had mean width 0.0945 and coverage 0.950; Phi had mean width 0.3287 and coverage 0.970 (versus conservative mean_square_region widths 0.1974 / 0.7249 and coverage 1.000).
  • Across an eight-condition normal-model check (2,000 sources per condition; 5–80 Persons; 2 x 2 to 2 x 20 source facets; zero/near-zero Person variance, dominant facets/interactions, and changed future counts), all-attempt 95% inclusion ranged from 0.9505 to 0.9885 for G and 0.948 to 1.000 for Phi (MC SE approx. 0.0049), with small-source Phi intervals spanning [0, 1] in over 90% of cases when source facet degrees of freedom were minimal.

Extended-nuisance score inversion (method = "score", crossed G)

  • Across six normal-model conditions and three future plans (360 independent sources per condition), true-value score-test acceptance ranged from 93.1% to 97.8% (MC SE 0.8–1.3 percentage points; lowest cell exact binomial 95% CI 89.9%–95.5%). Extending the same score rule to Phi produced very wide sets sensitive to few-df facet strata, so "score" is restricted to balanced two-crossed-facet G.

Restricted-likelihood profiles (method = "reml_profile")

  • Feasibility checks with 40 normal-model samples per assignment/population condition showed true-value likelihood-ratio inclusion of 92.5%–100% for positive components and 82.5%–100% in boundary populations (including SEM and bivariate covariance profiles, MC SE up to 6.0 percentage points). Asymptotic χ12\chi^2_1 cutoffs can undercover near zero-variance boundaries or few-level random facets, so "reml_profile" remains an explicit experimental option.

Measurement SEM (parm = "RelativeSEM" / "AbsoluteSEM", method = "mls")

  • Across nine normal-model source conditions (2,000 replications each; one-facet, crossed, and nested small/larger designs with three future plans) covering 51 positive-error targets, nominal 95% coverage ranged from 93.45% to 99.00% (MC SE 0.22–0.55 percentage points) with 99.75%–100% availability; the lowest cell (93.45%) occurred for AbsoluteSEM at 10 Persons, 2 raters, and 3 tasks projected to a 1 x 1 plan.

General nested approximate-F and region methods

  • Across three nested normal-model sources (2,000 samples each: 10 / 2 / 3, 60 / 4 / 8, and a residual-only boundary 10 / 2 / 3 model for Persons / children per parent / parents), interior approximate-F 95% coverage was 93.55%–96.45% (98.9%–100% available), whereas in the residual-only boundary source projected to 4 children and 6 parents, all-attempt coverage dropped to 62.85% (G) and 61.95% (Phi). A 200-sample mean_square_region check maintained 99.5%–100% availability with conservative widths sometimes exceeding 0.99.

Component-covariance delta intervals (method = "delta")

In 2,000 independent normal-model samples per incomplete source (retaining approx. 8/11 of cells; Person and residual variances 1.0, other components 0.2; all-attempt denominator), nominal 95% delta performance was:

Source Persons x measurement counts G returned (%) G covered (%) Phi returned (%) Phi covered (%)
One facet: 10 x 3 92.00 83.55 92.60 83.60
One facet: 60 x 8 100.00 95.65 100.00 95.25
Crossed: 10 x 2 x 3 78.95 78.30 86.45 82.90
Crossed: 30 x 4 x 5 100.00 93.90 100.00 91.10
Nested: 10 x 2 within 3 97.30 86.40 97.85 87.10
Nested: 40 x 3 within 6 100.00 94.55 100.00 91.75

Between-score Wishart GCI (confint.mfrm_multivariate_gstudy, method = "gci")

  • Across four 2,000-sample normal-model checks (8,000 pivotal draws each) for one-facet residual (10 x 2), crossed residual and Task (10 x 2 x 3), and crossed Rater (60 x 4 x 8) covariances, nominal 95% coverage was 94.65%, 94.80%, 99.65%, and 96.50% (MC SE 0.13–0.50 percentage points); blocks with 1 degree of freedom remain unavailable under Wishart GCI.

3. Small-sample binomial benchmark for common-plan JML expected scores

In ?confint.mfrm_fair_average, CIEligible remains FALSE for experimental "delta" and "refit" methods because short per-Person exposure limits normal and basic-bootstrap calibration even when local derivatives are exact:

  • In the binary special case with n=6n = 6 independent responses per Person, the Jeffreys expected-score estimator is (S+0.5)/7(S + 0.5) / 7 for S∼Bin(6,p)S \sim \mathrm{Bin}(6, p).
  • At p=0.5p = 0.5, the plug-in 95% delta interval covers only for S∈{2,3,4}S \in \{2, 3, 4\}, giving exact coverage 0.781250.78125 (0.78440.7844 at p=0.25p = 0.25).
  • Infinite-replication basic bootstrap refit quantiles for the same estimator yield exact coverage 0.781250.78125 at p=0.5p = 0.5 and 0.45270.4527 at p=0.10p = 0.10 (for S=0S = 0, the upper basic limit equals 0.5/70.5 / 7 because replicate estimates cannot fall below the estimator’s floor).
  • By contrast, method = "bounded" applies Hoeffding’s finite-sample inequality directly to observed bounded responses on declared rubrics without model extrapolation to unobserved plan cells.
